sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from FY2018 to FY2025, reaching $25.8 billion [F145][F8].
The path was not smooth: revenue jumped 22.3% in FY2022, fell 5.2% in FY2024 and rebounded 9.8% in FY2025 [D131][D201][D236].
The FY2024 decline came from lower storm and fuel cost recovery revenues at FPL [F7][D201][P35].
FY2025's rebound reflected higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel recovery [F8][D236][P21].
Operating income compounded faster at 9.9% [F146], but net income grew only 0.4% and diluted EPS fell 0.7% over the window [F147][F149].
FPL supplied 70.5% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.5pp of the 9.8% growth [D271][D273][D236].
FPL's revenue rose on higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues [S6][P21].
NEER's results rose on higher earnings from new investments, partly offset by higher financing costs [S29][P26].
Operating income grew 10.7% against revenue growth of 9.8%, an incremental margin of 34.8% [D237][D236][D256].
Net income still fell 1.6% and diluted EPS 2.1% as the diluted share count rose 0.6% [D238][D240][D251].
The FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% sits above the 30.3% window median but far below the 41.3% FY2023 high [F24][D300][D299].
The margin was essentially flat in FY2025, up 0.3pp, as operating costs grew 10.0% against revenue growth of 9.8% [D247][D249][D236].
D&A rose $951 million, mainly higher amortization of deferred storm costs from Hurricanes Debby, Helene and Milton [X32][P16].
The FY2025 effective tax rate fell to -17.7% on clean energy tax credits, which rose about $585 million [D226][P11].
Net margin of 26.5% trailed operating margin by 5.6pp, reflecting $3.75 billion of other expense [F40][D327][X64].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion was 1.83x net income in FY2025, below the 1.95x window median [F64][F32][D227][D319].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% while investing outflow reached $23.9 billion, leaving free cash flow deeply negative [D241][F72].
The swing from over- to under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million [P19].
D&A of $6.58 billion was 25.5% of revenue, so capex far exceeded depreciation [X32][D224].
Total debt reached $95.0 billion in FY2025 against $2.81 billion of cash, a net debt position of $92.2 billion [D230][D229][D231].
Net debt rose for a seventh straight year and equals 357.4% of revenue, the 0th percentile against three utilities peers whose median net cash is -235.4% of revenue [D231][D232][D328][D329].
Long-term debt grew 23.7% in FY2025 while equity grew 9.0% [D245][D244].
Dividends of $4.68 billion were funded alongside $23.4 billion of new debt issuance, and the diluted share count rose 0.6% [X82][X90][D251].
The current ratio is 0.60x, below 1.0x, though it is the window high and up from 0.36x in FY2018 [F128][D305][D304].
Net debt has risen every year to $92.2 billion, and leverage is the weakest in the peer group [D231][D328].
FY2025 net income fell on lower Corporate and Other results from non-qualifying hedge activity and higher debt balances [F32][D238][P8].
The effective tax rate swung -23.3pp to -17.7%, so net income now leans heavily on tax credits [D226][D191].
If the FY2026 operating margin holds above the 30.3% window median, the FY2023 spike looks like a one-off [F24][D300].
Watch whether net debt as a share of revenue moves back toward the FY2023 level of 283.3% from 357.4% [D162][D232].
Watch operating cash flow conversion against the 1.95x window median in the FY2026 10-K [D319].
